verdict.rationale: Angular's docs claim fine-grained reactivity via Signals, and hands-on users describe explicit component data flow through @Input/@Output and readable (events)/[attributes] binding syntax. That points to explicit, directional data flow, but nothing documents how developers trace state changes or how this replaces implicit two-way binding. The AngularJS digest and two-way-binding complaints concern the older framework and don't contradict this. Missing for 10: first-party docs on unidirectional data flow and state-change tracing or debugging, explicit treatment of how two-way binding is avoided or made explicit, and independent corroboration that Signals make state changes traceable.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trace state changes through explicit, predictable data flow instead of debugging implicit two-way bindings

citations.quote: fine-grained reactivity based on Angular Signals
